messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT — 5xx spike from model-serving after deploy at 08:23 UTC. Routing: production-us-east. Paging oncall: sarah (oncall). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploy-failure

sarah (oncall): I'm on it. seeing request errors in the metrics dashboard, 5xx rate jumped ~12% starting 08:23. grabbing logs now.

mike (eng-releases): I pushed the canary (release 2026.03.15-45) at 08:20, canary looked green for the first 10m. No manual feature flags changed.

jess (sre): throwing up tail of logs from model-serving:
```
2026-03-15T08:23:12Z ERROR handler.go:234 requestID=abcd status=500 err="KMS Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key"
stack=...
```

sarah (oncall): that looks like a KMS error during model key unwrap. Could be rotated key or permission. Are we reading KMS key ARN from an env var in the rollout?

mike (eng-releases): yes, release included a change to the MODEL_KMS_KEY env var to switch to the centrally-rotated key ARN (feature: key rotation integration). Canary used k8s secret 'model-kms-key-canary' which we thought matched prod.

raj (customer-ops): customer-impact check: we have ~2000 requests/min, about 240/min failing. A few enterprise customers reported timeouts to support. tagging priority P1 for potential wide impact.

jess (sre): quick mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag to disable new key usage (if we can avoid KMS call) 2) rollback to previous release 3) patch role/policy on KMS key. Which is fastest?

sarah (oncall): get feature flag kill-switch up first to stop further failures while we assess. mike, can you toggle? Which flag controls the key switch?

mike (eng-releases): flag is feature_flags.model_kms_rotation (console path: /flags/model_kms_rotation). toggling now.

mike (eng-releases): toggled -> OFF :white_check_mark: (via console).

infra-bot: feature_flags.model_kms_rotation set to false by mike (eng-releases) at 08:28 UTC.

jess (sre): after flag off, 5xx rate dropped to baseline within ~45s. Good — kill-switch worked for majority.

sarah (oncall): excellent. now we need root cause before unblocking. logs still show some pods failing with KMS error; maybe some replicas picked up new env var earlier and cached the key id.

mike (eng-releases): running rollout status: some pods were created with new secret reference: MODEL_KMS_KEY=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/old-key-id and others with arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/new-key-id. Canaries got old, prod nodes got new — looks like secret sync race during deploy.

jess (sre): here's the exact error from failing pod: "AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to use key arn:...:key/new-key-id" — key policy for new-key-id only includes the service principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-kms-access-prod but the nodes use role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-inference-prod (different role). The key policy was updated incorrectly.

mike (eng-releases): oh — while rotating keys we created a new KMS key and intended to add the inference role, but an automation step only stamped the release role. That explains the permission gap.

raj (customer-ops): impact summary for ops: 240/min failing during 08:23–08:28 (kill-switch), estimated customers affected: 12 customers (2 enterprise with SLA noise). Logged CS ticket numbers for follow-up.

sarah (oncall): remediation plan: A) revert the env var/secret across deployments OR B) patch key policy to include the correct role. Which to pick for minimal customer impact? Patching key policy is quick but requires AWS key admin steps and audit. Reverting rollout is safer.

mike (eng-releases): I'll trigger an immediate rollback to 2026.03.14-99 (previous stable). initiating rollback now.

deploy-bot: Rollback request accepted. Rolling back service model-serving to revision 2026.03.14-99. Start: 08:30 UTC.

infra-bot: kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-serving --to-revision=2026.03.14-99 executed by mike (eng-releases)

jess (sre): watching. after rollback completes, we should confirm all pods are using the previous k8s secret and env var references. Also validate token/cert rotation not affected.

sarah (oncall): handoff: I'm going to start incident timeline for postmortem. mike, you own rollback completion and validation. jess, you own logs/metrics validation. raj, keep customers updated with ETA. I'll stay until validation complete.

mike (eng-releases): rollback complete at 08:33 UTC. all pods now reference MODEL_KMS_KEY=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/old-key-id.

jess (sre): metrics look clean. 5xx returned to baseline within 90s after rollback fully rolled out. no remaining KMS errors in logs.

raj (customer-ops): customer notifications: sent initial status to impacted customers at 08:36. Will follow up with root cause summary and ETA for permanent fix.

sarah (oncall): containment achieved via feature flag + rollback. Impact window: 08:23 — 08:34 UTC (approx 11m). Impacted request percentage ~12% of traffic in that window. No data loss reported.

mike (eng-releases): immediate next steps: 1) block the broken key from being referenced in future releases (fail CI if MODEL_KMS_KEY doesn't match allowed-key-list) 2) fix automation to add the correct role to key policy during rotation 3) add canary checks to validate KMS Decrypt for sampled pods before promoting rollout.

jess (sre): also add a preflight that runs a synthetic decrypt against new key for a sample node. If AccessDenied, fail canary and stop rollout.

sarah (oncall): postmortem owner: mike (eng-releases). Please include timeline, root cause (secret sync + incorrect key policy), customer impact, and action items above. Set followup meeting 48 hours.

mike (eng-releases): will own. preliminary RCA draft by EOD.

infra-bot: Incident resolved: severity=P1 -> mitigated. Closed at 08:40 UTC by sarah (oncall).

sarah (oncall): closing thread here. good job team — quick kill-switch and rollback saved the day. :riot_face: (jk) :thumbsup:

raj (customer-ops): adding ticket links & support notes to the incident doc.

mike (eng-releases): will follow up with change to CI and automation PRs.

jess (sre): adding monitoring alert to detect sudden KMS AccessDenied spikes.

incident-bot: Note: postmortem template created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4312000000/postmortem
